To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the elastic nucleon scattering is a complicated process that cannot be described by the simple formula of West and Yennie, that the eikonal model seems to be more appropriate and that the predictions for LHC energy, which have been obtained on its basis, may be useful for the planned experiments.

the eikonal model of elastic nucleon collisions enables to determine physical characteristics (cross sections, total and differential, and luminosity) in impact parameter space and that the contemporary phenomenological models enable to predict some characteristics of the LHC collisions.
the elastic scattering of charged particles is a very complicated phenomenon and that it is not yet fully understood. [1]
In summary, our research is concerned with
a phenomenological analysis of elastic nucleon collisions at LHC energies and the possibility of using elastic nucleon-nucleon scattering to determine the luminosity at these energies.

the following topics: (a) the analysis of the existing phenomenological models of elastic scattering of charged nucleons, (b) the analysis of experimental data on elastic scattering at high energies, (c) the predictions for the LHC energy, (d) the determination of luminosity from elastic collisions, (e) the determination of the total cross-section of elastic collisions.

the following issues: - determination of the impact parameter distribution for elastic scattering, - determination of the luminosity from the elastic scattering cross section, - predictions of the total elastic and inelastic cross sections at the planned LHC energies.

the phenomenological models are not sufficient for precise description of elastic scattering.
the eikonal approach is more adequate to describe the elastic collisions of charged particles, however the West-Yennie formula is still useful in the region of small impact parameters.

the eikonal model is more appropriate than the West and Yennie model, but it is necessary to take into account the influence of the nuclear medium on the scattering processes in order to obtain reliable predictions.
